purpose: Nicardipine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and chest pain (angina). Keeping your blood pressure under control helps protect your heart, kidneys, and brain from damage. It may be given as a pill you take at home or as an IV drip in the hospital for more serious situations.
how_it_works: Your blood vessels have tiny channels that let calcium flow in, which causes the vessel walls to tighten and squeeze. Nicardipine blocks those calcium channels so your blood vessels can relax and widen. When your vessels are more relaxed, your heart does not have to work as hard and your blood pressure goes down.
common_side_effects: Flushing or feeling warm in your face, headache, dizziness, swelling in your ankles or feet, fast heartbeat (palpitations), nausea, and feeling tired. Most of these are mild and often improve as your body gets used to the medicine.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause your blood pressure to spike or trigger chest pain. Tell your doctor if you have heart failure, liver disease, or kidney disease, as your dose may need adjustment. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as it can raise the level of this drug in your blood and increase side effects. Stand up slowly to avoid dizziness from a sudden drop in blood pressure.
typical_dosing: For high blood pressure, the usual starting dose of the regular capsule is 20 mg taken three times a day. The extended-release capsule (SR) is usually 30 mg taken twice a day. Your doctor may gradually increase your dose based on how well your blood pressure is controlled. Always take it exactly as your doctor tells you.
